zh.title: OmniXtreme: Breaking the Generality Barrier in High-Dynamic Humanoid Control
zh.authors: Yunshen Wang, Shaohang Zhu, Peiyuan Zhi, Yuhan Li, Jiaxin Li, Yong-Lu Li, Yuchen Xiao, Xingxing Wang, Baoxiong Jia, Siyuan Huang
zh.institutions: 北京通用人工智能研究院通用人工智能国家重点实验室；北京通用人工智能研究院与宇树科技具身智能及人形机器人联合实验室；上海交通大学；中国科学技术大学；宇树科技；华中科技大学；北京理工大学
zh.takeaway: 先把单动作专家蒸馏成统一 Flow Matching 跟踪策略，再用执行器感知的残差 PPO 适配高动态真机动作。
zh.mainContent: OmniXtreme 先为参考动作训练单动作 PPO 专家，再通过 DAgger 和条件 Flow Matching 将专家反馈动作蒸馏成统一基础策略。冻结基础策略后，残差 PPO 在执行器力矩—转速包络、非线性摩擦和域随机化下学习硬件适配。Unitree G1 上覆盖翻转、杂技、舞蹈和武术，157 次真机测试的总体成功率为 91.08%。
innovations: 提出一个两阶段高动态人形机器人控制框架，将大规模动作表示学习与真实硬件执行适配分开优化：预训练阶段学习统一基础策略，后训练阶段仅学习执行器感知的残差修正。
采用 specialist-to-unified 的训练范式：先使用 BeyondMimic 风格的 PPO 为每个参考动作训练专家，再在统一策略自身访问的状态上使用 DAgger 获取专家动作标签。
使用条件 Flow Matching 蒸馏专家动作：网络学习从高斯噪声到专家动作的条件速度场，并通过有限步 Euler 积分生成最终动作。
在 Flow Matching 策略中使用 Transformer 编码当前本体状态、参考运动命令和 15 步历史信息，再与带噪动作嵌入和 Flow 时间嵌入共同预测动作空间速度场。
在残差后训练中显式加入电机力矩—转速工作包络、平滑库仑摩擦、黏性摩擦、强域随机化以及膝关节负机械功率惩罚，以提高高冲击动作的真实硬件可执行性。
需要批判性看待的是。
implementation: 动作数据来自经过 Unitree G1 重定向的 LAFAN1、AMASS、MimicKit 和 Reallusion 动作库；论文另外整理了包含约 60 个高动态动作的 XtremeMotion 集合。
每个参考动作分别训练一个 PPO 专家策略。专家 actor 和 critic 均为隐藏层维度 [512, 256, 128] 的 ELU MLP，并采用非对称 actor-critic 训练。
专家 actor 输入包括参考关节位置与速度、躯干相对参考的位置和 6D 姿态误差、基座线速度与角速度、相对默认姿态的关节位置、关节速度和上一时刻动作。
专家策略输出归一化动作 \(a\)，该动作通过 \(q_{\mathrm{tar}} = q_0 + \alpha \odot a\) 映射为目标关节位置，再由 PD 控制器计算关节力矩；因此专家动作在控制意义上是目标关节位置偏移命令，而不是关节速度。
Flow 预训练首先让当前统一策略在仿真中执行，再在学生访问的状态上查询对应动作专家，构造包含状态、参考动作和专家动作标签的 DAgger 数据。
Flow Matching 使用线性概率路径 \(a_t = (1-t)a_{\mathrm{expert}} + t\epsilon\)，其中 \(\epsilon\) 服从标准高斯分布，\(t\) 从 Beta 分布采样；训练目标为最小化 \(\lVert v_\theta(a_t,t,o) - (\epsilon-a_{\mathrm{expert}}) \rVert^2\)。
Flow Matching 中的 \(v_\theta\) 是生成过程在动作空间中的速度场，不是机器人关节角速度；推理时从高斯噪声开始，沿反向时间执行 Euler 积分得到最终基础动作。
Flow 策略将当前本体状态 p 和运动命令 c 各编码为一个 token，将 15 步历史分别编码为 15 个 token，共形成 17 个 token。每类输入先经过两层、每层 256 单元的 ReLU MLP，再送入 Transformer encoder。
Transformer 输出经过全局平均池化和线性投影形成 1024 维状态表示；带噪动作和 Flow 时间分别编码为 1024 维表示，三者拼接后通过隐藏层维度 [2048, 2048, 2048] 的 MLP 输出 Flow 速度场。
基础 Flow 策略完成后被冻结，残差策略使用隐藏层维度 [1024, 512, 256, 128, 64] 的 MLP，并通过 PPO 学习与基础动作同维度的修正动作。
残差策略输入包含机器人本体感知、参考躯干姿态、参考关节位置和速度、上一时刻最终动作，以及当前 Flow 基础动作；最终动作等于基础动作与残差动作之和。
执行器模型根据关节转速动态限制可用力矩，并加入平滑库仑摩擦和黏性摩擦；负功率惩罚主要用于抑制膝关节在高冲击落地阶段产生过大的再生制动力。
真实部署使用 Unitree G1 的关节状态和骨盆 IMU，通过 FK 构造观测。Flow 基础策略和残差策略导出为 ONNX，并使用 ONNX Runtime 与 TensorRT 在 Jetson Orin NX 上板载运行。
部署时每个控制周期使用 5 次 Flow ODE Euler 积分，输出 29 维全身动作；论文报告端到端推理延迟约 10 ms，控制周期为 20 ms，即 50 Hz。

en.title: OmniXtreme: Breaking the Generality Barrier in High-Dynamic Humanoid Control
en.authors: Yunshen Wang, Shaohang Zhu, Peiyuan Zhi, Yuhan Li, Jiaxin Li, Yong-Lu Li, Yuchen Xiao, Xingxing Wang, Baoxiong Jia, Siyuan Huang
en.institutions: State Key Laboratory of General Artificial Intelligence, Beijing Institute for General Artificial Intelligence; Joint Laboratory of Embodied AI and Humanoid Robots, BIGAI and Unitree Robotics; Shanghai Jiao Tong University; University of Science and Technology of China; Unitree Robotics; Huazhong University of Science and Technology; Beijing Institute of Technology
en.takeaway: Distills single-motion experts into a unified flow-matching tracker, then uses actuator-aware residual PPO for highly dynamic real-robot motion.
en.mainContent: OmniXtreme trains single-motion PPO experts and distills their feedback actions into a unified base policy with DAgger and conditional flow matching. A residual PPO policy then adapts the frozen base under actuator torque–speed envelopes, nonlinear friction, and randomization. Unitree G1 tests span flips, acrobatics, dance, and martial arts, with 91.08% success over 157 real-robot trials.
innovations: A two-stage framework that separates large-scale motion representation learning from hardware-oriented physical refinement: a unified base tracker is pretrained first, followed by residual actuation-aware post-training.
A specialist-to-unified pipeline in which motion-specific PPO teachers are trained first and queried on states visited by the unified learner through DAgger.
Conditional Flow Matching is used to distill expert actions by learning a velocity field that transports Gaussian noise toward the expert action distribution through finite-step Euler integration.

A Transformer encodes current proprioception, the reference motion command, and a 15-step proprioceptive history before the resulting state embedding is combined with noisy-action and flow-time embeddings.

The residual post-training environment explicitly models torque-speed envelopes, smoothed Coulomb friction, viscous friction, stronger domain randomization, and negative knee mechanical power penalties for high-impact motions.

A key limitation is that the paper does not compare against a matched Transformer and DAgger policy trained by direct expert-action regression, so the gain cannot be cleanly attributed to Flow Matching itself.
implementation: Motion data are collected from Unitree-retargeted LAFAN1, AMASS, MimicKit, and Reallusion libraries. The paper additionally curates an XtremeMotion set containing roughly 60 challenging high-dynamic motions.
A separate PPO specialist is trained for each reference motion. The teacher actor and critic are ELU MLPs with hidden dimensions [512, 256, 128] and use an asymmetric actor-critic setup.

Teacher actor observations contain reference joint positions and velocities, torso position and 6D orientation errors, base linear and angular velocity, joint positions relative to the default pose, joint velocities, and the previous action.

The teacher outputs a normalized action \(a\) that is converted into desired joint positions through \(q_{\mathrm{tar}} = q_0 + \alpha \odot a\) and then tracked by a PD controller. Thus, the expert action is a desired joint-position offset command rather than a physical joint velocity.
For Flow pretraining, the current unified policy is rolled out in simulation and the corresponding motion specialist labels the states visited by the learner, producing DAgger supervision.

The Flow Matching path is \(a_t = (1-t)a_{\mathrm{expert}} + t\epsilon\), where \(\epsilon\) is Gaussian noise and \(t\) is sampled from a Beta distribution. The objective minimizes \(\lVert v_\theta(a_t,t,o) - (\epsilon-a_{\mathrm{expert}}) \rVert^2\).

The predicted \(v_\theta\) is a velocity in the artificial action-generation flow, not the robot joint velocity. At inference, the policy starts from Gaussian noise and integrates the velocity field backward in flow time.

Current proprioception p and motion command c are each mapped to one token, while the 15-step history is mapped to 15 tokens, resulting in a sequence of 17 tokens. Dedicated preprocessing MLPs contain two 256-unit ReLU layers.
The token sequence is processed by a Transformer encoder, followed by global average pooling and a linear projection to a 1024-dimensional state embedding.

The noisy action and flow timestep are separately embedded into 1024-dimensional representations. The state, action, and time embeddings are concatenated and passed through an MLP with hidden dimensions [2048, 2048, 2048] to predict the flow velocity.
The pretrained Flow policy is frozen during post-training. The residual policy is an MLP with hidden dimensions [1024, 512, 256, 128, 64] and is optimized with PPO.

Residual actor inputs include proprioception, relative torso orientation, reference joint positions and velocities, the previous final action, and the current Flow base action. The final action is the sum of the base and residual actions.

The actuator model applies a speed-dependent torque envelope and nonlinear friction after torque clipping. A negative mechanical power penalty is selectively applied to the knee joints to reduce unsafe regenerative braking during impact landings.

For real-robot deployment, joint states and pelvis IMU measurements are used to construct observations, while torso rotation is obtained through forward kinematics. The base and residual policies are exported to ONNX and executed with ONNX Runtime and TensorRT on the onboard Jetson Orin NX.

The deployed base policy uses five Euler ODE integration steps and outputs a 29-dimensional whole-body action. The paper reports approximately 10 ms end-to-end inference latency at a 20 ms control period, corresponding to 50 Hz.

zh.title: HIL: Hybrid Imitation Learning for Dynamic Athletic Control
zh.authors: Jiashun Wang, Yifeng Jiang, Haotian Zhang, Chen Tessler, Davis Rempe, Jessica Hodgins, Xue Bin Peng
zh.institutions: Carnegie Mellon University；NVIDIA；Simon Fraser University
zh.status: 全文已精读（依据正文与附录，并按上传模板更新）
zh.takeaway: 保留 motion tracking 的技能复习，同时加入 task + AMP rollout，共同训练一个能适应障碍的 actor。
zh.mainContent: HIL 先训练 goal-conditioned motion tracker，再同时保留 tracking 环境与 task + AMP 环境，两组 rollout 更新同一个 actor。持续跟踪维持技能覆盖，任务与风格奖励帮助策略适应障碍和组合技能。跑酷实验展示较高的技能准确率和较低的跟踪误差，同时呈现与任务完成率之间的权衡。
innovations: 论文的核心贡献是一个两阶段混合训练范式，而不是新的 PPO 或对抗学习算法：第一阶段训练 motion tracking policy，第二阶段在 AMP 任务适应过程中持续保留 motion tracking 环境，使参考技能不断向共享 actor 提供监督，减轻遗忘和模式坍缩。
为 tracking mode 和 adversarial task mode 设计统一的 goal-conditioned observation。策略在两种模式下都接收角色状态和任务条件，而不依赖只在参考轨迹中存在的显式 phase 或完整 future target pose，因此两组环境能够真正共享同一个 actor。
在第二阶段使用并行多任务环境：一半环境执行逐帧 motion tracking，另一半环境执行 task reward + AMP style reward，来自两类环境的 PPO 样本被混合用于更新同一个策略。
跑酷任务中的 discriminator 同时观察过去 10 步角色状态和局部场景点云，使其不仅判断动作是否接近参考运动分布，也判断动作是否适合当前障碍几何。
使用 Perturbed State Initialization 对参考初始状态加入高斯扰动，扩大 tracking policy 的恢复范围，并缓解前一个技能终止状态与后一个技能起始状态不匹配造成的过渡困难。
implementation: 数据准备：作者从 YouTube 收集 19 个跑酷视频片段，总计约 30 秒、覆盖 15 种技能；先使用 TRAM 恢复人体运动，人工用盒体近似障碍场景，再使用 physics-based motion tracker 修正碰撞、抖动和滑动。修正后的运动用于计算 tracking reward、执行 PSI 初始化，并作为 AMP discriminator 的正样本。

第一阶段——Motion Tracking Pretraining：使用约 40 亿个样本训练一个 goal-conditioned tracking policy。跑酷策略输入当前角色状态 \(s_t\)、局部场景点云 \(c_t\) 和目标位置 \(l_t\)，其中 tracking 阶段的 \(l_t\) 从参考轨迹未来 1–2 秒的 root position 中采样。策略通过逐帧位置、旋转、线速度、角速度和 root height 跟踪奖励学习各个独立技能。
第二阶段——Hybrid Training：从第一阶段得到的 actor 权重继续训练约 20 亿个样本。4096 个并行环境中，一半运行 motion tracking mode，另一半运行 adversarial imitation learning mode；它们不是分别训练两个策略，而是产生两类 rollout 后共同更新同一个 actor。

第二阶段的 tracking 环境仍然读取参考运动并计算 \(0.5r_t^{\mathrm{track}}+0.5r_t^{\mathrm{style}}\)，作用是持续 rehearsal，防止 actor 在任务适应过程中遗忘复杂动作。adversarial task 环境不进行逐帧参考跟踪，而计算 \(0.5r_t^{\mathrm{task}}+0.5r_t^{\mathrm{style}}\)，其中 task reward 鼓励接近和穿越目标障碍，style reward 由 AMP discriminator 提供。
Actor 在两种模式下使用完全相同的输入接口，并且不接收 tracking/task mode 标识。Critic 额外接收二值模式变量 \(k_t\)，用于区分两种不同的奖励和 return 分布；该变量不输入 actor，以避免策略显式分裂成 tracking policy 和 task policy。
Discriminator 的正样本来自修正后的参考运动，负样本来自 policy rollout。跑酷 discriminator 输入连续 10 步的 root 速度、关节旋转与速度、末端位置以及局部场景点云，并输出 style reward；场景条件用于约束不同障碍应匹配不同的动作技能。
策略网络使用状态 MLP、目标 MLP 和 PointNet 编码输入，再送入 2 层、2 头、latent dimension 为 256 的 Transformer。策略输出固定标准差为 0.055 的高斯动作分布，动作表示目标关节位置，并通过 PD 控制器转换为关节力矩。
训练使用 Isaac Gym、PPO 和 GAE，仿真频率为 120 Hz，策略频率为 30 Hz，使用 4096 个并行环境和 4 张 NVIDIA V100。tracking 与 task/style reward 在第二阶段的权重均为 0.5。
部署时不再存在两组环境或两种模式，只保留训练完成的 actor 和 PD controller。Actor 根据当前角色状态、局部点云和外部目标位置输出目标关节位置；部署不需要参考运动、tracking reward、discriminator、critic、PSI 或模式变量。
实验中 HIL 的 skill accuracy 为 0.66、tracking error 为 0.31、task completion 为 0.74；AMP warm start 的 task completion 为 0.85，但 skill accuracy 和 tracking quality 更差。因此 HIL 的结果应理解为用部分纯任务性能换取更好的技能覆盖和参考动作保真度。

en.title: HIL: Hybrid Imitation Learning for Dynamic Athletic Control
en.authors: Jiashun Wang, Yifeng Jiang, Haotian Zhang, Chen Tessler, Davis Rempe, Jessica Hodgins, Xue Bin Peng
en.institutions: Carnegie Mellon University; NVIDIA; Simon Fraser University
en.takeaway: Retains motion-tracking rehearsal while adding task-plus-AMP rollouts to train one actor that adapts to obstacles.
en.mainContent: HIL first trains a goal-conditioned tracker, then updates one actor with both tracking and task-plus-AMP rollouts. Tracking rehearsal preserves skills while task and style rewards support obstacle adaptation and skill composition. Parkour experiments show better skill accuracy and lower tracking error, alongside a trade-off in task completion.
innovations: The core contribution is a two-stage hybrid training recipe rather than a new PPO or adversarial-learning algorithm: after motion-tracking pretraining, reference tracking remains active throughout AMP-based task adaptation, continuously supervising the shared actor and reducing forgetting and mode collapse.

A unified goal-conditioned observation space is used in both tracking and adversarial task modes. The policy receives character state and task conditions in both modes instead of relying on tracking-only inputs such as an explicit phase variable or a full future target pose.

During the second stage, half of the parallel environments perform frame-wise motion tracking and half perform task-conditioned AMP. Rollouts from both groups are combined to update one shared policy rather than separate tracking and task policies.

For parkour, the discriminator observes a 10-step history of character states together with local scene point clouds, allowing the style reward to evaluate both motion naturalness and compatibility with the current obstacle geometry.

Perturbed State Initialization adds Gaussian noise to reference initial states to enlarge the tracking policy's recovery region and improve transitions when the ending state of one skill does not match the nominal starting state of another.
implementation: Data preparation: the authors collect 19 YouTube parkour clips totaling roughly 30 seconds and covering 15 skills. TRAM is used to recover human motion, obstacle scenes are manually approximated with boxes, and a physics-based motion tracker refines collisions, jitter, and sliding. The refined motions are used for tracking rewards, PSI initialization, and positive discriminator samples.

Stage 1 — Motion Tracking Pretraining: approximately 4 billion samples are used to train a goal-conditioned tracking policy. For parkour, the policy receives character state \(s_t\), local scene point cloud \(c_t\), and target location \(l_t\), where the tracking target is sampled from the reference root position 1–2 seconds in the future. Frame-wise position, rotation, velocity, angular-velocity, and root-height rewards teach individual skills.

Stage 2 — Hybrid Training: training continues from the Stage-1 actor for approximately 2 billion samples. Of 4096 parallel environments, half run motion tracking and half run adversarial imitation tasks. These environments do not train separate policies; their rollouts jointly update the same actor.

In Stage 2, tracking environments retain access to reference motions and use \(0.5r_t^{\mathrm{track}}+0.5r_t^{\mathrm{style}}\). This branch serves as persistent rehearsal that prevents the actor from forgetting complex skills during adaptation. Adversarial task environments do not perform frame-wise tracking and instead use \(0.5r_t^{\mathrm{task}}+0.5r_t^{\mathrm{style}}\), where the task reward encourages obstacle traversal and the style reward is produced by the AMP discriminator.

The actor uses the same observation interface in both modes and does not receive a tracking/task mode indicator. The critic additionally receives a binary variable \(k_t\) to distinguish the two reward and return distributions; the indicator is withheld from the actor to discourage an explicit split into separate tracking and task policies.

The discriminator is trained with refined reference transitions as positive samples and policy-generated transitions as negative samples. For parkour, it observes 10 consecutive steps of root velocity, joint rotations and velocities, end-effector positions, and local scene point clouds.

The policy uses state and target MLP encoders and a PointNet, followed by a 2-layer, 2-head Transformer with latent dimension 256. It outputs a Gaussian distribution over desired joint positions with fixed standard deviation 0.055, and PD controllers convert desired positions into torques.

Training uses Isaac Gym, PPO, and GAE at 120 Hz simulation and 30 Hz policy control, with 4096 parallel environments on four NVIDIA V100 GPUs. During hybrid training, both the tracking/task term and the style term have weight 0.5.

At deployment, the environment split and both training modes disappear. Only the trained actor and PD controllers are retained: current character state, local point cloud, and an externally supplied target location are mapped to desired joint positions. Reference motions, tracking rewards, the discriminator, critic, PSI, and the mode indicator are not required.

HIL reports a skill accuracy of 0.66, tracking error of 0.31, and task completion of 0.74. Warm-start AMP reaches a higher task completion of 0.85 but has worse skill coverage and tracking quality, so HIL should be interpreted as trading some pure task performance for better diversity and reference-motion fidelity.

zh.title: Universal Humanoid Motion Representations for Physics-Based Control
zh.authors: Zhengyi Luo, Jinkun Cao, Josh Merel, Alexander Winkler, Jing Huang, Kris Kitani, Weipeng Xu
zh.institutions: Meta Reality Labs Research；Carnegie Mellon University
zh.takeaway: 把 PHC+ 的运动跟踪能力蒸馏成 32 维共享潜在动作空间，让下游 PPO 在人类运动先验中探索。
zh.mainContent: PULSE 用 PHC+ 跟踪清理后的 AMASS 动作，再在线蒸馏编码器、解码器和本体状态条件先验，得到 32 维连续概率潜空间。下游任务冻结共享先验与解码器，分别训练高层 PPO 策略输出潜变量残差。速度控制、伸手、击打、复杂地形和 VR 跟踪实验展示了这一接口对探索效率和运动自然度的帮助。
innovations: 把大规模物理跟踪能力压缩为连续低维技能接口。
本体状态条件先验提供随当前身体状态变化的运动偏好。
通过高层潜变量残差复用固定低层控制器。
implementation: 训练 PHC+ motion tracker，作为在线动作蒸馏的教师。
学生控制仿真，教师在学生访问的状态标注动作；编码器、解码器和条件先验通过动作匹配与 KL 正则联合训练。
下游 PPO 策略读取任务目标与身体状态，输出 32 维 latent residual；固定解码器把潜变量变成闭环关节动作。

en.title: Universal Humanoid Motion Representations for Physics-Based Control
en.authors: Zhengyi Luo, Jinkun Cao, Josh Merel, Alexander Winkler, Jing Huang, Kris Kitani, Weipeng Xu
en.institutions: Meta Reality Labs Research; Carnegie Mellon University
en.takeaway: Distills PHC+ motion tracking into a shared 32-dimensional latent action space for downstream PPO exploration.
en.mainContent: PULSE tracks cleaned AMASS motion with PHC+ and distills an encoder, decoder, and state-conditioned prior into a 32-dimensional probabilistic latent space. Downstream tasks freeze the shared prior and decoder and train separate high-level PPO policies to produce latent residuals. Speed control, reaching, striking, terrain, and VR tracking demonstrate benefits for exploration and natural movement.
innovations: Compresses large-scale physical tracking into a continuous low-dimensional skill interface.
A proprioceptive prior supplies motion preferences conditioned on the current body state.
Reuses a fixed low-level controller through high-level latent residuals.
implementation: Trains a PHC+ motion tracker as the teacher for online action distillation.
The student controls the simulation and the teacher labels its visited states. Action matching and KL regularization train the encoder, decoder, and conditional prior.
Each downstream PPO policy observes task goals and body state and outputs a 32-dimensional latent residual; the fixed decoder produces feedback joint actions.

zh.title: GPC: Large-Scale Generative Pretraining for Transferable Motor Control
zh.authors: Yi Shi, Yifeng Jiang, Chen Tessler, Xue Bin Peng
zh.institutions: Simon Fraser University; NVIDIA
zh.takeaway: 先用物理跟踪学出 FSQ 技能 token，再用 Transformer 生成 token，通过 CoLA 和任务微调复用运动先验。
zh.mainContent: GPC 先用 PPO 联合训练带 FSQ 瓶颈的参考编码器与物理解码器，将物理可执行的运动压缩为离散技能。随后以 token 为监督信号预训练状态条件自回归 Transformer，并用 CoLA、可选 SFT 和 RLFT 适配目标到达、转向、轨迹跟踪及交互任务。仿真角色实验中，FSQ 在 Bones 上达到 99.98% 跟踪成功率和 34.90 mm MPJPE；9.8 m/s 推扰下 GPC 的存活率为 52.5%，CVAE 为 3.1%。
innovations: 在物理运动跟踪中端到端学习 FSQ 离散技能，使表示与执行器共同训练。
以分组 token 构建状态条件自回归运动先验。
用条件低秩适配 CoLA 将任务信息接入冻结的预训练骨干。
implementation: 参考窗口取未来第 1、2、5、7、12、18、25 帧；编码器输出 40 维 latent，经 FSQ 量化后送入物理解码器。
FSQ 使用固定标量量化等级；每 5 维打包成一组，总共 8 个 token，平衡序列长度与词表规模。
PPO 跟踪目标包含全局关节位置与旋转、根高度、关节速度和角速度；actor 的大型隐藏矩阵使用 Muon，其他参数与 critic 使用 AdamW。
冻结物理解码器，以状态与技能 token 训练 Transformer；每个控制时刻生成 8 个分组 token，再解码为关节动作。
CoLA 使用 rank 64、缩放 128 的低秩分支，任务观测生成 FiLM 参数；下游通过监督或任务奖励更新适配参数。

en.title: GPC: Large-Scale Generative Pretraining for Transferable Motor Control
en.authors: Yi Shi, Yifeng Jiang, Chen Tessler, Xue Bin Peng
en.institutions: Simon Fraser University; NVIDIA
en.takeaway: Learns FSQ skill tokens through physical tracking, generates them with a Transformer, and adapts the motion prior with CoLA and task fine-tuning.
en.mainContent: GPC jointly trains an FSQ-bottleneck reference encoder and physical decoder with PPO, compressing executable motion into discrete skills. A state-conditioned autoregressive Transformer learns these tokens, followed by CoLA, optional SFT, and RLFT for reaching, steering, path tracking, and interactions. In simulated-character experiments, FSQ reaches 99.98% tracking success and 34.90 mm MPJPE on Bones; under a 9.8 m/s push, GPC survives at 52.5% versus 3.1% for a CVAE.
innovations: Learns FSQ skills end to end in physical tracking, shaping the representation jointly with execution.
Builds a state-conditioned autoregressive motion prior over grouped tokens.
Injects task information into the frozen pretrained backbone with conditional low-rank adaptation (CoLA).
implementation: Encodes reference frames 1, 2, 5, 7, 12, 18, and 25 into a 40-dimensional latent, quantized by FSQ and passed to the physical decoder.
FSQ uses fixed scalar levels and packs every five dimensions into one group, yielding eight tokens and trading sequence length against vocabulary size.
PPO tracks global joint positions and rotations, root height, and joint velocities. Muon optimizes large hidden actor matrices; AdamW handles other parameters and the critic.
Freezes the physical decoder and trains the Transformer on states and skill tokens; each control timestep generates eight grouped tokens and decodes them into joint actions.
CoLA uses rank 64 and scale 128 low-rank branches with task-conditioned FiLM parameters; supervision or task rewards update downstream adaptation parameters.

zh.title: ASE: Large-Scale Reusable Adversarial Skill Embeddings for Physically Simulated Characters
zh.authors: Xue Bin Peng, Yunrong Guo, Lina Halper, Sergey Levine, Sanja Fidler
zh.institutions: University of California, Berkeley; NVIDIA; University of Toronto
zh.takeaway: 先用对抗模仿、技能识别奖励和多样性正则学会可控的连续技能，再冻结低层，让高层根据任务目标选择技能。
zh.mainContent: ASE 从无技能标签的动作库学习潜变量条件低层策略：对抗模仿维持自然运动，互信息与多样性目标鼓励不同 latent 产生可区分的行为。预训练期间持续切换 latent，学习技能保持与过渡；下游任务冻结低层策略，训练高层策略选择技能向量。一个共享低层模型用于 Reach、Speed、Steering、Location 和 Strike 等仿真角色任务。
innovations: 将无标注动作库组织为可复用的连续技能空间。
联合对抗模仿、互信息和多样性目标，学习自然且可区分的潜变量行为。
在预训练中改变技能条件，为技能切换提供经验。
implementation: 使用 187 段、约 30 分钟的 Reallusion 动作，包含行走、跑步、转向、蹲伏、挥剑和盾击。
低层策略读取 120 维本体状态和 64 维单位球面技能向量，输出 31 维关节目标，由 PD 控制器执行。
预训练①采样与交互：将标准高斯样本归一化，得到单位球面均匀先验中的技能向量；低层策略 \(\pi(a\mid s,z)\) 在仿真中执行动作，记录状态转移和所用技能。每个 latent 保持 1–150 个低层步后重新采样，一个 episode 内也切换技能，以学习衔接。（第 6 页式 11；第 7 页算法 1；附录 A）
预训练②计算奖励：\(r_t=-\log(1-D(s_t,s_{t+1}))+\beta\log q(z_t\mid s_t,s_{t+1})\)。判别器奖励鼓励动作符合数据风格，编码器奖励鼓励行为能辨认出所选技能；预训练不使用下游任务奖励，\(\beta=0.5\)。（第 5 页式 10；表 2）
预训练③更新编码器与判别器：先用策略生成的转移及技能标签训练 q 反推 latent，再用动作库转移作为正样本、策略转移作为负样本训练 D，并在动作库样本上加入梯度惩罚。q 不负责先把参考动作编码成技能；实现中 q 与 D 共享网络主干、使用不同输出头。（第 6 页式 13–14；第 7 页算法 1；第 8 页图 5、§8.2）
预训练④更新策略与价值函数：用上述奖励计算 GAE 优势，通过 PPO 更新低层策略，通过 TD(λ) 更新 V(s,z)。额外的 diversity 正则让同一状态下动作分布的 KL 散度与 latent 的余弦距离相匹配；它只用于策略梯度更新，不加进每步奖励。重复采集轨迹、更新 q/D、更新 π/V。（第 6 页式 15；第 7 页算法 1、§6.6）
跌倒恢复：预训练时每个 episode 有 10% 概率从随机倒地状态开始；倒地状态由随机高度和朝向的空中掉落生成，使恢复能力随低层技能一起迁移。（第 6 页 §6.5）
任务训练①选择技能：冻结预训练低层策略 π，为每个任务训练独立高层 PPO 及其价值函数。高层读取当前状态 s 和任务目标 g，输出高斯分布中的未归一化向量，再归一化为 z 交给低层；低层继续根据当前状态闭环输出关节动作。（第 7 页 §7.1、图 3；第 9 页 §8.2）
任务训练②计算奖励：\(r_t=w_G r_t^G-w_S\log(1-D(s_t,s_{t+1}))\)，任务奖励权重为 0.9、风格奖励权重为 0.1。D 保持冻结，仅前向计算风格分数；此阶段不再使用 q 的技能识别奖励，也不需要动作库。（第 8 页式 16；附录 A 表 3）
控制频率：任务训练高层以 6 Hz 更新技能，低层以 30 Hz 输出动作，每个高层技能保持 5 个低层步；物理仿真以 120 Hz 积分。（第 10 页 §10.1；第 18 页附录 A）
部署使用高层策略和低层策略的反馈闭环。论文观察到部分动作覆盖不足和偶发抽动，体现技能分布学习的实际质量。

en.title: ASE: Large-Scale Reusable Adversarial Skill Embeddings for Physically Simulated Characters
en.authors: Xue Bin Peng, Yunrong Guo, Lina Halper, Sergey Levine, Sanja Fidler
en.institutions: University of California, Berkeley; NVIDIA; University of Toronto
en.takeaway: Pretrains controllable continuous skills with adversarial imitation, skill-identification rewards, and diversity regularization, then freezes the low-level policy and learns task-conditioned skill selection.
en.mainContent: ASE learns a latent-conditioned low-level policy from an unlabeled motion library. Adversarial imitation maintains natural motion, while mutual-information and diversity objectives encourage distinguishable latent-conditioned behaviors. Changing latents during pretraining teaches both skill persistence and transitions; downstream tasks train high-level policies over the frozen low-level model for reaching, speed, steering, location, and striking.
innovations: Turns an unlabeled motion library into a reusable continuous skill space.
Combines adversarial imitation, mutual information, and diversity objectives for natural, distinguishable latent behaviors.
Changes skill conditions during pretraining to supply transition experience.
implementation: Uses 187 Reallusion clips totaling about 30 minutes of walking, running, turning, crouching, sword swings, and shield bashes.
The low-level policy observes 120-dimensional proprioception and a 64-dimensional unit-sphere skill vector and outputs 31-dimensional joint targets for PD control.

Pretraining 1 — sampling and interaction: normalizes standard Gaussian samples to draw skills uniformly on the unit sphere. The low-level policy \(\pi(a\mid s,z)\) acts in simulation and records transitions and their conditioning skills. Each latent lasts 1–150 low-level steps before resampling; skills also change within episodes to teach transitions. (p. 6, Eq. 11; p. 7, Algorithm 1; Appendix A)

Pretraining 2 — rewards: \(r_t=-\log(1-D(s_t,s_{t+1}))+\beta\log q(z_t\mid s_t,s_{t+1})\). The discriminator rewards dataset-like behavior; the encoder rewards behavior that identifies the chosen skill. Pretraining uses no downstream task reward, and \(\beta=0.5\). (p. 5, Eq. 10; Table 2)

Pretraining 3 — encoder and discriminator updates: first trains q to recover latents from policy-generated transitions and their skill labels, then trains D with motion-data transitions as positives and policy transitions as negatives, adding a gradient penalty on motion-data samples. q does not first encode reference clips into skills. The implementation shares a backbone between q and D with separate output heads. (p. 6, Eqs. 13–14; p. 7, Algorithm 1; p. 8, Fig. 5 and §8.2)

Pretraining 4 — policy and value updates: computes GAE advantages from these rewards, updates the low-level policy with PPO, and updates V(s,z) with TD(λ). An additional diversity regularizer matches action-distribution KL divergence at the same state to cosine distance between latents; it applies only during policy gradient updates, not as a per-step reward. Repeats rollout collection, q/D updates, and π/V updates. (p. 6, Eq. 15; p. 7, Algorithm 1 and §6.6)

Recovery: initializes 10% of pretraining episodes in random fallen states generated by dropping the character from random heights and orientations, so recovery transfers with the low-level skills. (p. 6, §6.5)

Task training 1 — skill selection: freezes the pretrained low-level policy π and trains a separate high-level PPO policy and value function for each task. The high-level policy observes state s and task goal g, samples an unnormalized Gaussian vector, and normalizes it into z for the low-level policy, which continues closed-loop joint control using the current state. (p. 7, §7.1 and Fig. 3; p. 9, §8.2)

Task training 2 — rewards: \(r_t=w_G r_t^G-w_S\log(1-D(s_t,s_{t+1}))\), with task and style weights 0.9 and 0.1. D stays frozen and only supplies style scores through forward evaluation; this stage uses neither q-based skill-identification rewards nor the motion dataset. (p. 8, Eq. 16; Appendix A, Table 3)

Control rates: the high-level policy selects skills at 6 Hz and the low-level policy produces actions at 30 Hz, holding each high-level skill for five low-level steps; physics runs at 120 Hz. (p. 10, §10.1; p. 18, Appendix A)
Deployment uses the high- and low-level policies in a feedback loop. The paper observes incomplete motion coverage and occasional twitching in the learned skill distribution.

zh.title: BFM-Zero: A Promptable Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control Using Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
zh.authors: Yitang Li, Zhengyi Luo, Tonghe Zhang, Cunxi Dai, Anssi Kanervisto, Andrea Tirinzoni, Haoyang Weng, Kris Kitani, Mateusz Guzek, Ahmed Touati, Alessandro Lazaric, Matteo Pirotta, Guanya Shi
zh.institutions: Carnegie Mellon University; Meta
zh.takeaway: 把 FB-CPR 的奖励、目标和动作提示接口部署到真实 G1：共享 latent、历史反馈、大规模 off-policy 训练与执行安全正则。
zh.mainContent: BFM-Zero 将 reward、goal 和 motion prompt 编码到共享的 256 维任务空间，由同一个 latent-conditioned actor 执行全身控制。训练基于 FB-CPR，结合大规模并行 off-policy 交互、mocap 条件判别器、历史依赖的非对称 actor-critic 与辅助安全 critic。模型在真实 Unitree G1 上展示多种提示方式下的运动控制，是 FB 路线走向实体人形机器人的系统实现。
innovations: 统一 reward、goal 和 motion 三种数值提示的任务编码与策略调用。
通过历史反馈和非对称学习，把仿真训练信息转化为真机可用的控制策略。
将大规模 off-policy FB-CPR 训练、域随机化与辅助安全目标组合为 G1 部署管线。
implementation: F、B 和 actor 共享任务向量语义；奖励经 B 加权聚合，目标与参考动作也通过同一表示空间形成控制条件。
mocap 条件判别器把示范行为与潜变量联系起来，辅助 critic 学习控制代价并约束 actor 更新。
actor 读取真实可用的本体历史，critic 在训练时读取特权信息；交互数据存入 replay buffer，用于并行 off-policy 更新。
域随机化、观测噪声和随机推扰覆盖动力学误差与外部扰动；部署时使用冻结策略，根据提示生成任务条件。

en.title: BFM-Zero: A Promptable Behavioral Foundation Model for Humanoid Control Using Unsupervised Reinforcement Learning
en.authors: Yitang Li, Zhengyi Luo, Tonghe Zhang, Cunxi Dai, Anssi Kanervisto, Andrea Tirinzoni, Haoyang Weng, Kris Kitani, Mateusz Guzek, Ahmed Touati, Alessandro Lazaric, Matteo Pirotta, Guanya Shi
en.institutions: Carnegie Mellon University; Meta
en.takeaway: Brings FB-CPR reward, goal, and motion prompting to the real G1 through shared latents, history-based feedback, large-scale off-policy training, and execution regularization.
en.mainContent: BFM-Zero encodes reward, goal, and motion prompts in a shared 256-dimensional task space and executes them with one latent-conditioned actor. Training combines FB-CPR with large-scale parallel off-policy interaction, a mocap-conditioned discriminator, history-dependent asymmetric actor–critic learning, and an auxiliary safety critic. Real Unitree G1 demonstrations bring the FB control interface to a physical humanoid.
innovations: Unifies task encoding and policy execution for numerical reward, goal, and motion prompts.
Uses history-based asymmetric learning to train a policy with observations available on the real robot.
Combines large-scale off-policy FB-CPR training, domain randomization, and auxiliary safety objectives into a G1 deployment pipeline.
implementation: F, B, and the actor share task-vector semantics; B aggregates reward features, while goals and reference motions form conditions in the same representation space.
A mocap-conditioned discriminator associates demonstrations with latents, while an auxiliary critic learns control costs and regularizes actor updates.
The actor observes deployable proprioceptive history; the critic receives privileged training information. Parallel interaction supplies replay for off-policy updates.
Domain randomization, observation noise, and random pushes cover dynamics mismatch and disturbances. Deployment uses a frozen policy conditioned on the chosen prompt.

zh.title: Zero-Shot Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Behavioral Foundation Models
zh.authors: Andrea Tirinzoni, Ahmed Touati, Jesse Farebrother, Mateusz Guzek, Anssi Kanervisto, Yingchen Xu, Alessandro Lazaric, Matteo Pirotta
zh.institutions: FAIR at Meta；Mila；McGill University；University College London (UCL)
zh.takeaway: FB-CPR 把 MoCap 行为分布对齐到 FB 潜空间，让同一个策略通过奖励、目标姿态或参考动作直接调用。
zh.mainContent: Meta Motivo 使用 FB-CPR 预训练全身人形控制器：FB 学习长期访问表示，潜变量条件判别器把无动作标签的 MoCap 轨迹与同一任务空间联系起来。奖励函数、目标姿态和参考运动都可转换成 B 表示空间中的任务条件，调用同一个 actor。模型在 AMASS 与 SMPL 仿真人形上训练，七项归一化指标的平均得分达到任务专用上界的 73.4%。
innovations: 用潜变量条件行为分布匹配，将 MoCap 示范与 FB 的奖励可编程能力结合。
统一奖励优化、姿态到达与运动跟踪的任务表示和控制策略。
通过无动作标签的状态轨迹学习自然运动，将示范中的行为覆盖引入无奖励预训练。
implementation: 预训练联合更新 F、B、actor 与条件判别器；示范提供状态序列，环境交互提供动作与真实状态转移。
CPR 根据潜变量条件区分示范与策略行为，为 actor 提供行为分布匹配目标；FB 的 TD 目标学习不同策略条件下的长期访问。
新奖励用奖励加权的 B 特征构造任务向量；姿态目标使用目标表征，参考动作通过随时间变化的潜变量调用同一个 actor。
部署阶段冻结模型，读取当前本体状态与任务向量；实验在固定仿真人形上评估奖励任务、目标控制和跟踪。

en.title: Zero-Shot Whole-Body Humanoid Control via Behavioral Foundation Models
en.authors: Andrea Tirinzoni, Ahmed Touati, Jesse Farebrother, Mateusz Guzek, Anssi Kanervisto, Yingchen Xu, Alessandro Lazaric, Matteo Pirotta
en.institutions: FAIR at Meta; Mila; McGill University; University College London (UCL)
en.takeaway: FB-CPR aligns mocap behavior distributions with the FB latent space so one policy can be directly prompted by rewards, poses, or reference motions.
en.mainContent: Meta Motivo pretrains a whole-body humanoid controller with FB-CPR: FB learns long-term occupancy representations, and a latent-conditioned discriminator connects action-free mocap trajectories to the same task space. Rewards, target poses, and reference motions become conditions for one actor. Trained on AMASS with a simulated SMPL humanoid, the model averages 73.4% of task-specific upper bounds across seven normalized metrics.
innovations: Combines latent-conditioned behavior matching from mocap with the reward-conditioning interface of FB.
Shares task representations and a policy across reward optimization, pose reaching, and motion tracking.
Uses action-free state trajectories to bring natural-motion coverage into reward-free pretraining.
implementation: Jointly trains F, B, the actor, and a conditional discriminator. Demonstrations provide state sequences; environment interaction supplies actions and state transitions.
CPR distinguishes demonstrated and policy-generated behavior under latent conditions; FB TD targets learn long-term occupancy for those conditions.
Reward-weighted B features encode new rewards; pose features encode targets; time-varying latents prompt the same actor with reference motion.
Deployment freezes the model and supplies current proprioception and a task vector. Experiments evaluate reward tasks, goal control, and tracking with a fixed simulated humanoid.

zh.title: Heracles: Bridging Precise Tracking and Generative Synthesis for General Humanoid Control
zh.authors: Zelin Tao, Zeran Su, Peiran Liu, Jingkai Sun, Wenqiang Que, Jiahao Ma, Jialin Yu, Jiahang Cao, Pihai Sun, Hao Liang, Gang Han, Wen Zhao, Zhiyuan Xu, Jian Tang, Qiang Zhang, Yijie Guo
zh.institutions: X-Humanoid（北京人形机器人创新中心有限公司）
zh.takeaway: 用当前真实状态条件化的 Flow Matching 中间件在线改写短期参考，再让低层 tracker 执行和恢复。
zh.mainContent: Heracles 在高层运动命令和低层 tracker 之间加入状态条件 Flow Matching 中间件，用当前构型作为锚点生成 0.2 秒、8 个关键帧的短期参考。接近原动作时保留参考，偏离时改写为恢复轨迹，再由 iFSQ PPO tracker 执行。G1 的 101 条未见序列 sim2sim 测试完成率为 90.6%，跌倒恢复子集为 90.0%，并展示真机动作与恢复。
innovations: 系统层面的核心创新是把 state-conditioned generative middleware 插入“原始运动参考—低层物理跟踪器”之间，使参考轨迹本身能随实时物理状态闭环变化，并避免显式 tracking/recovery 模式切换。
采用以当前 generator-space 构型为锚点的 geometric residual parameterization：\(\tau_{t,k}=p_t+r_{t,k}\)。模型生成的是各关键帧相对当前构型的变化量，而不是绝对姿态；近参考时残差趋小，严重偏离时残差可编码协调的恢复过渡。
在现有 Flow Matching 与 Transformer 基础上组合了首 token inpainting、directional warm start 和固定时域 receding-horizon replanning，以较少 ODE 步数生成连续、朝向目标的短期恢复轨迹。
生成器训练加入仅扰动起始状态的 asymmetric noisy-state augmentation，以及由姿态相关 Jacobian 近似 \(\mathrm{diag}(J^\top J)\) 得到的 kinematics-aware loss weighting；消融实验表明二者对部署鲁棒性和几何敏感关节的学习均有明显作用。
低层 Tracker 的系统性改进包括 iFSQ 离散运动表示、共享 token 的 reconstruction/action 双解码头，以及带平滑难度传播的 adaptive motion sampling。Flow Matching、AdaLN Transformer、PPO 和 iFSQ 本身并非本文从零提出，创新主要体现在面向通用人形跟踪与恢复的表示、训练设计和层级整合。
implementation: 整体训练不是把生成器与 Tracker 端到端联合反向传播。Physics Tracker 在 IsaacLab 中用 asymmetric actor-critic PPO 训练；其 motion encoder、iFSQ quantizer、reconstruction decoder 与 action decoder 在 Tracker 内共享编码路径并联合优化。之后，Flow Matching trajectory generator 使用同一运动语料构造的轨迹对离线训练。

生成器训练目标：先以当前构型为基线构造并归一化真实 residual \(x_0\)，采样同形状高斯噪声 \(x_1\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\)，再随机采样 Flow 坐标 \(s\) 并构造 \(x_s=(1-s)x_0+s x_1\)。AdaLN Transformer 接收 \((x_s,s,[p_t,m_t])\)，学习速度目标 \(x_1-x_0\)；也就是程序在推理时按预设 schedule 改变 \(s\)，网络负责预测每一步 residual 张量应该如何移动。

生成器为 6 个 attention blocks、4 个 heads、hidden dimension 512 的 AdaLN Transformer，共 22.9 M 参数；输出覆盖 0.2 s 固定规划时域的 \(K=8\) 个均匀关键帧，其中首帧锚定当前状态。论文训练 38D 与 35D 两种状态表示：38D 包含 29D 关节位置、3D root position 和 6D root orientation，可修正全局位置漂移但需要全局定位；35D 去掉 root position，可仅依赖关节编码器与 IMU 部署，但将全局平移交给外部参考源。
生成器数据来自 LAFAN1、100STYLE、SnapMoGen、AMASS 和自有 MoCap。每个训练样本从运动段起点提取未来固定时域的 8 个关键帧，以受噪声扰动的起始状态和运动段终点 reference command 作为条件；Jacobian 权重在数据构建时用可微 FK 预计算并缓存。

部署时先构造 \(r_k^{\mathrm{init}}=\frac{k}{K-1}(m_t-p_t)\)，在 \(s=0.9\) 将其与高斯噪声混合，然后由程序自动执行 5 个 Euler steps，把 \(s\) 从 0.9 积分到 0。每步对首 residual token 施加 inpainting，使最终首帧锚定当前构型；8 个关键帧随后用 joint-position cubic spline 与 root-orientation SLERP 稠密化。

生成式中间件每 2 个控制步重规划一次，即 0.04 s / 25 Hz；Physics Tracker 在 50 Hz 执行稠密参考。Tracker 使用 10 帧 proprioceptive history 与 10 帧 future reference window，经 iFSQ motion token 和 action decoder 输出 29D target joint positions，底层 PD 在 200 Hz 产生关节力矩。
Tracker 训练使用 16,384 个 IsaacLab 并行环境和单张 NVIDIA A100 80 GB，仿真频率 200 Hz、策略频率 50 Hz，并随机化摩擦、质心偏置、参考命令和外部推扰。测试在 MuJoCo 中使用 101 条 held-out motion sequences；官方项目页截至 2026-07-29 仍将代码标为 Coming Soon。

en.title: Heracles: Bridging Precise Tracking and Generative Synthesis for General Humanoid Control
en.authors: Zelin Tao, Zeran Su, Peiran Liu, Jingkai Sun, Wenqiang Que, Jiahao Ma, Jialin Yu, Jiahang Cao, Pihai Sun, Hao Liang, Gang Han, Wen Zhao, Zhiyuan Xu, Jian Tang, Qiang Zhang, Yijie Guo
en.institutions: X-Humanoid (Beijing Innovation Center of Humanoid Robotics Co., Ltd.)
en.takeaway: A state-conditioned flow-matching middleware rewrites short-term references online for low-level tracking and recovery.
en.mainContent: Heracles places state-conditioned flow-matching middleware between motion commands and a low-level tracker. Anchored to the current configuration, it generates eight keyframes over 0.2 seconds, preserving nearby references and rewriting mismatched ones for recovery. An iFSQ PPO tracker executes them; G1 sim-to-sim tests reach 90.6% completion over 101 unseen sequences and 90.0% on the recovery subset, with real-robot demonstrations.
innovations: The main system-level contribution is a state-conditioned generative middleware between the original reference and the low-level physics tracker, allowing the reference itself to adapt in closed loop to the robot's physical state without an explicit tracking-versus-recovery mode switch.

A geometric residual parameterization anchored at the current generator-space configuration, \(\tau_{t,k}=p_t+r_{t,k}\), makes the generator predict changes relative to the present configuration rather than absolute poses. Residuals remain small near nominal tracking but can encode coordinated recovery transitions under severe deviations.

On top of existing Flow Matching and Transformer components, the method combines first-token inpainting, a directional warm start, and fixed-horizon receding-horizon replanning to produce continuous, target-directed recovery trajectories with few ODE steps.

Generator training adds asymmetric noisy-state augmentation and a pose-dependent kinematics-aware loss weight based on an approximation of \(\mathrm{diag}(J^\top J)\). Ablations show that both substantially affect deployment robustness and learning of geometrically sensitive joints.

The low-level tracker is strengthened with an iFSQ discrete motion representation, reconstruction and action heads sharing the same token, and adaptive motion sampling with smoothed difficulty propagation. Flow Matching, AdaLN Transformers, PPO, and iFSQ are existing ingredients; the contribution is primarily their task-specific representation, training design, and hierarchical integration.
implementation: The generator and tracker are not trained through a single end-to-end objective. The physics tracker is trained in IsaacLab with asymmetric actor-critic PPO; its motion encoder, iFSQ quantizer, reconstruction decoder, and action decoder share an encoding path and are jointly optimized inside the tracker. The Flow Matching trajectory generator is then trained offline on trajectory tuples extracted from the same motion corpus.

For generator training, a normalized ground-truth residual is used as \(x_0\), same-shaped Gaussian noise \(x_1\sim\mathcal N(0,I)\) is sampled, and a random flow coordinate \(s\) yields \(x_s=(1-s)x_0+s x_1\). The AdaLN Transformer receives \((x_s,s,[p_t,m_t])\) and regresses the velocity target \(x_1-x_0\): at inference the program advances the prescribed schedule for \(s\), while the network predicts how the residual tensor should move at each step.

The generator is a 22.9 M-parameter AdaLN Transformer with six attention blocks, four heads, and hidden dimension 512. It predicts \(K=8\) uniformly spaced keyframes over a fixed 0.2 s horizon, with the first keyframe anchored to the current state. Two state representations are trained: 38D with 29D joint positions, 3D root position, and 6D root orientation, which can correct global drift but requires global localization; and 35D without root position, which can use joint encoders and an IMU only but delegates global translation to the external reference source.

Generator data come from LAFAN1, 100STYLE, SnapMoGen, AMASS, and proprietary MoCap. Each tuple extracts eight keyframes over a fixed future window, conditions on a noisy start state and the segment-end reference command, and uses Jacobian weights precomputed and cached through differentiable forward kinematics.

At deployment, the solver forms \(r_k^{\mathrm{init}}=\frac{k}{K-1}(m_t-p_t)\), mixes it with Gaussian noise at \(s=0.9\), and automatically performs five Euler steps from \(s=0.9\) to 0. First-token inpainting anchors the final first residual to the current configuration; joint-position cubic splines and root-orientation SLERP then densify the eight keyframes.

The middleware replans every two control steps, or 0.04 s / 25 Hz, while the physics tracker executes the dense reference at 50 Hz. The tracker uses a 10-frame proprioceptive history and a 10-frame future reference window, then outputs 29D target joint positions through the iFSQ motion token and action decoder; a low-level PD controller runs at 200 Hz.

Tracker training uses 16,384 parallel IsaacLab environments on one NVIDIA A100 80 GB GPU, with 200 Hz simulation and 50 Hz policy control, plus randomization of friction, center-of-mass offsets, reference commands, and external pushes. Evaluation uses 101 held-out motion sequences in MuJoCo; the official project page still marked the code as Coming Soon on 2026-07-29.

papers.venue: ACM Transactions on Graphics (Proc. SIGGRAPH Asia 2024)

zh.title: MaskedMimic: Unified Physics-Based Character Control Through Masked Motion Inpainting
zh.authors: Chen Tessler, Yunrong Guo, Ofir Nabati, Gal Chechik, Xue Bin Peng
zh.institutions: NVIDIA；Bar-Ilan University；Simon Fraser University
zh.takeaway: 把完整运动教师蒸馏成带条件先验的 VAE，用部分关节、文本和物体目标驱动同一个物理动作补全控制器。
zh.mainContent: MaskedMimic 将部分关节、文本、物体和地形目标统一为闭环 motion inpainting。先用 RL 训练读取完整未来运动的教师，再以结构化 mask、在线动作蒸馏和条件 VAE 学习从稀疏目标直接生成动作。AMASS 全身跟踪成功率为 99.2%、MPJPE 为 35.1 mm；VR 稀疏跟踪成功率为 98.1%，路径、到达和坐下通过部分目标与 FSM 调用同一策略。
innovations: 系统级地将全身跟踪、VR 稀疏跟踪、关键帧补间、路径控制、文本控制和静态物体交互统一为同一个物理运动补全接口；RL motion tracking、DAgger、VAE 和 Transformer 等单独组件并非本文首创。
设计跨时间保持一致的结构化掩码：近期目标的关节可见模式以 98% 概率沿用，加入完全遮挡的 time gap，并随机隐藏文本、物体和远期目标，避免模型通过多帧可见关节的并集泄露完整运动。
采用特权后验与目标条件先验的残差 C-VAE：后验读取未遮挡的完整未来运动以确定当前训练样本的具体 latent，先验只读取部署时可用的部分目标，并通过 KL 对齐学习从欠约束输入预测可执行动作分布。
将 PULSE 的运动先验与任务特定高层策略合并为直接读取用户目标的条件先验，使下游任务不再需要单独的 PPO/RL 训练；代价是任务必须能表达为模型已支持的部分目标，并可能需要人工 FSM 调度。
implementation: 角色基于 neutral SMPL，具有 69 个自由度；状态空间为 358 维，动作是以指数映射编码的 69 维 PD 目标。当前姿态、速度、未来目标和场景均规范化到角色根部局部坐标系，根高度单独保留。
第一阶段使用 A2C 训练全约束教师：Transformer actor 读取当前状态、完整未来全身姿态和局部高度图，MLP critic 估计价值；奖励包含全局关节位置、旋转、根高度、关节速度、角速度和能耗六项。训练场景由平地、不规则地形和物体 playground 组成，并使用 early termination 与按平地失败率进行的 prioritized motion sampling。
第二阶段冻结教师并让学生控制仿真。结构化 mask 将完整目标变为部分目标；先验读取当前状态、部分关键帧、历史姿态、XCLIP 文本、物体和高度图，后验额外读取未遮挡未来姿态；decoder 根据当前状态、地形和 latent 输出 PD 动作。教师在学生访问的同一状态上读取完整目标并标注动作，训练目标由教师动作行为克隆损失和后验—先验 KL 损失组成。

先验采用 4 层、4 头 Transformer，模型维度 512、FFN 维度 1024，无 dropout，输出 64 维 Gaussian latent；各模态编码器为隐藏层 [256, 256] 的 MLP，后验编码器和 decoder 均使用 [1024, 1024, 1024] MLP。训练时 episode 内固定重参数化噪声 epsilon，部署时可取先验均值获得稳定结果或采样获得多样性。
学生使用 11 个未来目标：前 10 个为连续近期帧，第 11 个为随机远期目标；历史输入从过去 40 帧中每 8 帧取一个，共 5 个姿态。物体由 8 个三维包围盒角点、6D 朝向和类别索引表示，地形使用点距 10 cm 的 16×16 高度图，文本使用 512 维 XCLIP 嵌入。
训练数据聚合 AMASS、HumanML3D 和 SAMP，并进行 AMASS 过滤、左右镜像和同类别物体随机替换。论文报告使用 16,384 个 Isaac Gym 并行环境和 4 张 A100，训练约 14 天；全约束教师约 300 亿步，MaskedMimic 约 100 亿步，策略运行于 30 Hz，物理仿真运行于 120 Hz。
部署时删除全约束教师和特权后验，仅保留先验与 decoder。路径、steering、reach 和 sit 等任务通过外部 FSM 构造或切换部分目标；因此无需任务特定再训练，但并未消除任务特定的目标、阈值和状态机设计。
定量结果包括：AMASS 测试集全身跟踪 99.2% 成功率、35.1 mm MPJPE；VR 跟踪 98.1% 成功率、58.1 mm 全身 MPJPE 和 45.8 mm 观测关节误差；不规则地形上的全身与 VR 成功率分别为 95.4% 和 93.6%；测试坐具上的坐下成功率为 96.9%。主要定量评估使用先验均值，随机采样的多样性—成功率权衡未被量化。

en.title: MaskedMimic: Unified Physics-Based Character Control Through Masked Motion Inpainting
en.authors: Chen Tessler, Yunrong Guo, Ofir Nabati, Gal Chechik, Xue Bin Peng
en.institutions: NVIDIA; Bar-Ilan University; Simon Fraser University
en.takeaway: Distills a full-motion teacher into a conditional-prior VAE so partial joints, text, and object goals drive one physical motion-inpainting controller.
en.mainContent: MaskedMimic unifies partial joints, text, objects, and terrain as closed-loop motion inpainting. A full-motion RL teacher is distilled with structured masks, online action labels, and a conditional VAE to generate actions directly from sparse goals. It reaches 99.2% full-body tracking success and 35.1 mm MPJPE on AMASS, and 98.1% VR tracking success; partial targets and FSMs invoke the same policy for paths, reaching, and sitting.
innovations: At the system level, it unifies full-body tracking, sparse VR tracking, keyframe inbetweening, path control, text control, and static-object interaction under one physics-based motion-inpainting interface; the individual components such as RL motion tracking, DAgger, VAEs, and Transformers are not themselves new.

It introduces temporally structured masking: near-term targets retain the previous joint-visibility pattern with 98% probability, fully masked time gaps are inserted, and text, objects, and long-term targets are randomly hidden, preventing the model from recovering the full motion through the union of independently visible joints across frames.

It uses a residual C-VAE with a privileged posterior and a goal-conditioned prior: the posterior observes the unmasked future motion to identify the concrete latent for each training example, while the prior observes only deployment-time partial goals and learns through KL alignment to predict a distribution of executable motions from underspecified inputs.

It merges PULSE's motion prior and task-specific high-level policy into a conditional prior that directly consumes user goals, removing separate PPO/RL training for downstream tasks; the tradeoff is that tasks must be expressible through supported partial goals and may still require a manually designed FSM.
implementation: The character uses the neutral SMPL body with 69 degrees of freedom; the state space is 358-dimensional, and the action is a 69-dimensional PD target encoded with exponential maps. Current poses, velocities, future targets, and scene observations are canonicalized in the character's root-local frame, while root height is retained separately.

The first stage trains a fully constrained teacher with A2C: a Transformer actor consumes the current state, complete future full-body poses, and a local heightmap, while an MLP critic estimates value; the reward contains six terms for global joint position, rotation, root height, joint velocity, angular velocity, and energy. The training scene contains flat ground, irregular terrain, and an object playground, with early termination and prioritized motion sampling based on flat-ground failures.

The second stage freezes the teacher and lets the student control the simulation. Structured masking converts complete goals into partial goals; the prior consumes the current state, partial keyframes, pose history, XCLIP text, objects, and the heightmap, while the posterior additionally observes unmasked future poses; the decoder outputs PD actions from the current state, terrain, and latent. The teacher reads the complete goal at the same student-visited state to label actions, and training combines behavioral cloning of teacher actions with posterior-prior KL alignment.

The prior is a 4-layer, 4-head Transformer with model dimension 512, FFN dimension 1024, no dropout, and a 64-dimensional Gaussian latent; modality encoders are MLPs with hidden sizes [256, 256], while the posterior encoder and decoder use [1024, 1024, 1024] MLPs. Reparameterization noise epsilon is fixed within each episode during training; inference can use the prior mean for stable behavior or sample for diversity.

The student uses 11 future targets: the first 10 are consecutive near-term frames, and the 11th is a random long-term target; pose history consists of 5 poses sampled every 8 frames from the preceding 40 frames. Objects are represented by eight 3D bounding-box corners, a 6D orientation, and a category index; terrain uses a 16×16 heightmap with 10 cm spacing, and text uses a 512-dimensional XCLIP embedding.

Training aggregates AMASS, HumanML3D, and SAMP, with AMASS filtering, left-right mirroring, and random replacement of objects within the same class. The paper reports 16,384 parallel Isaac Gym environments on four A100 GPUs for approximately 14 days; the fully constrained teacher uses about 30 billion steps and MaskedMimic about 10 billion, with the policy running at 30 Hz and physics simulation at 120 Hz.

At deployment, the fully constrained teacher and privileged posterior are removed, leaving only the prior and decoder. Tasks such as path following, steering, reaching, and sitting are implemented by an external FSM that constructs or switches partial goals; thus task-specific retraining is eliminated, but task-specific goal, threshold, and state-machine engineering remains.

Quantitative results include 99.2% success and 35.1 mm MPJPE for full-body tracking on the AMASS test set; 98.1% success, 58.1 mm full-body MPJPE, and 45.8 mm observed-joint error for VR tracking; 95.4% and 93.6% success for full-body and VR tracking on irregular terrain; and 96.9% sitting success on held-out seating objects. Major quantitative evaluations use the prior mean, and the diversity-success tradeoff under random sampling is not quantified.

zh.title: M3imic: Learning a Versatile Whole-Body Controller for Multimodal Motion Mimicking
zh.authors: Zuxing Lu, Ziang Zheng, Yao Lyu, Jingyu Liu, Feihong Zhang, Song Lu, Xin Yuan, Changyin Sun, Xingxing Zuo, Shengbo Eben Li
zh.institutions: 东南大学自动化学院；清华大学车辆与运载学院；穆罕默德·本·扎耶德人工智能大学机器人学系
zh.takeaway: 将机器人关节、人体姿态和稀疏末端目标对齐到共享 latent，统一密集跟踪与稀疏控制。
zh.mainContent: M3imic 将机器人关节角、SMPL-X 人体姿态和五个末端位姿分别编码为共享的 64 维潜在命令。物理跟踪、模态重建、latent 对齐和机器人空间一致性目标共同训练一个全身控制器。模型用 LAFAN1 与 100STYLE 训练，在未见 OMOMO 上末端模态成功率为 98.42%，并在真实 G1 上展示零样本迁移和光学动捕遥操作。
innovations: 为机器人关节角、SMPL-X 人体姿态和末端位姿分别设计编码器，将三种异构参考映射到连续的 64 维共享潜在命令空间，而不是先统一为显式关节轨迹或简单拼接带掩码的命令向量。
联合使用模态内重建损失、成对潜变量对齐损失，以及通过机器人解码器 D_r 计算的机器人空间一致性损失，使不同模态保留自身信息的同时具有共同的机器人控制语义。
将表示学习与物理运动跟踪强化学习组成单阶段训练框架，部署时只需选择对应模态编码器并复用同一个 Action Decoder，无需为每种输入模态重新训练策略；末端模式不需要部署时显式 IK，但训练数据仍依赖离线 GMR 重定向。
使用基于一秒动作片段终止失败率 EMA 的课程采样，在均匀采样与困难片段采样之间逐步过渡，并截断极端困难片段的采样概率。
系统性比较三种部署模态，观察到机器人关节参考具有更好的姿态和关节跟踪精度，而稀疏末端参考在动作分布变化下具有更高的成功率；主要贡献属于多模态表示与全身控制的系统整合，而非新的稳定性或收敛理论。
implementation: 数据预处理首先对人体动作进行筛选和 SMPL-X 整理，再通过 GMR 重定向到 29-DoF Unitree G1，形成时间对齐的机器人关节角、人体姿态和五个末端位姿三种参考。
机器人参考 q_t 为 29 维关节角；人体参考由 21 个关节的 6D rotation representation 构成；末端参考包含双手、双脚和胸部，每个末端由 3 维根坐标系相对位置和 6D 旋转表示构成。
每个控制时刻使用 H=10、采样间隔 Δ=2 的参考窗口，即索引 t、t+2 至 t+18。三个输入窗口分别为 10×29、10×21×6 和 10×5×9，并由模态专属 MLP 编码为 64 维潜变量。
三个模态解码器分别执行模态内重建；潜变量对齐损失最小化 z_r、z_h、z_e 的成对距离；一致性损失比较 D_r(z_r)、D_r(z_h) 和 D_r(z_e)，将机器人关节空间作为跨模态规范语义。
actor 输入潜在命令以及根姿态误差、基座角速度、实际关节角、关节速度和上一时刻动作；它刻意排除全局根位置与根线速度。critic 额外使用根位置误差、完整 body link 位置和姿态以及根线速度等仿真特权信息，部署时删除 critic。
总训练目标为策略损失与多模态自编码器损失之和。策略项采用 PPO 风格 clipped surrogate objective，包含 actor、value 和 entropy 项，实验部分称使用 RAD optimizer。
跟踪奖励包括根速度、根姿态、全身位置、全身姿态、全身线速度和全身角速度；正奖励权重依次为 0.5、0.5、1.0、1.0、1.0 和 1.0。正则项包括权重 -0.1 的动作变化、权重 -10.0 的关节越界和权重 -0.1 的碰撞惩罚。
课程学习将轨迹切分为一秒片段，以终止失败率 EMA 表示难度，并使用 P_final=αP_uniform+(1-α)clip(P_failure,0,P_max) 采样。消融实验设置 α_min=0.2、P_max=0.05。
Sim-to-Real 训练随机化包括摩擦、外部推力、基座质心、基座质量、默认关节位置及姿态、角速度、关节位置和关节速度噪声。正文还提到 link mass、inertia、joint damping 和 motor strength，但表格没有给出相应范围。
训练数据为 LAFAN1 和 100STYLE，未见动作测试使用 OMOMO test subset。课程、数据规模和网络规模消融在 4 张 RTX 4090 上训练 50000 iterations；标准 MLP 配置为 512、256、128，大网络为 1024、512、256。
在训练数据上，M3imic 达到 99.54% 成功率、46.05 mm MPKPE、0.112 rad MPJAE 和 0.256 m/s 根速度误差。在 OMOMO 上，机器人参考模式的 MPKPE 和 MPJAE 最低，分别为 71.52 mm 和 0.139 rad；末端模式以 98.42% 获得最高成功率，但 MPKPE 和 MPJAE 略高。
真机光学动捕实验中，机器人参考模式与末端模式的 MPKPE 分别为 41.63 mm 和 43.22 mm，MPJAE 分别为 0.095 rad 和 0.105 rad。

en.title: M3imic: Learning a Versatile Whole-Body Controller for Multimodal Motion Mimicking
en.authors: Zuxing Lu, Ziang Zheng, Yao Lyu, Jingyu Liu, Feihong Zhang, Song Lu, Xin Yuan, Changyin Sun, Xingxing Zuo, Shengbo Eben Li
en.institutions: School of Automation, Southeast University; School of Vehicle and Mobility, Tsinghua University; Department of Robotics, Mohamed Bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence
en.takeaway: Aligns robot joints, human poses, and sparse endpoint targets in one latent space for dense tracking and sparse control.
en.mainContent: M3imic encodes robot joints, SMPL-X poses, and five endpoint poses into a shared 64-dimensional command space. Physical tracking, reconstruction, latent alignment, and robot-space consistency train one whole-body controller. Trained on LAFAN1 and 100STYLE, its endpoint mode reaches 98.42% success on unseen OMOMO motion, with zero-shot G1 deployment and optical-mocap teleoperation.
innovations: It introduces separate encoders for robot joint angles, SMPL-X human poses, and end-effector poses, mapping the heterogeneous references into a continuous shared 64-dimensional latent command space instead of converting all commands into explicit joint trajectories or concatenating masked command vectors.

It combines within-modality reconstruction, pairwise latent alignment, and robot-space consistency through the robot decoder D_r so that each modality retains its own information while acquiring shared robot-control semantics.

It jointly trains representation learning and physics-based motion tracking in a single-stage framework. At deployment, a modality-specific encoder is paired with the same Action Decoder without modality-specific policy retraining; the end-effector mode avoids explicit runtime IK, although training data still depend on offline GMR retargeting.

It uses curriculum sampling based on an EMA of termination failure rates for one-second motion segments, gradually shifting from uniform sampling toward difficult segments while clipping extremely difficult cases.

It systematically compares the three deployment modalities and observes that robot-joint references provide better pose and joint tracking fidelity, whereas sparse end-effector references yield higher success under motion-distribution shift. The contribution is primarily a systems integration of multimodal representation learning and whole-body control rather than a new stability or convergence theory.
implementation: Human motion is filtered and processed in SMPL-X, then retargeted to the 29-DoF Unitree G1 with GMR to produce temporally aligned robot-joint, human-pose, and five-end-effector references.

The robot reference q_t contains 29 joint angles. The human reference contains 21 joints represented with 6D rotations. The end-effector reference contains both hands, both feet, and the chest, with each pose represented by a 3D root-relative position and a 6D rotation.

At each control step, the encoders receive a reference horizon with H=10 and sampling interval Δ=2, covering indices t, t+2 through t+18. The three input sizes are 10×29, 10×21×6, and 10×5×9, and each modality-specific MLP produces a 64-dimensional latent code. The control period is not reported, so the physical duration of this future window and its causal handling in online teleoperation are unknown.

Three modality decoders perform within-modality reconstruction. The alignment loss minimizes pairwise distances among z_r, z_h, and z_e, while the consistency loss compares D_r(z_r), D_r(z_h), and D_r(z_e), using robot joint space as the canonical cross-modal semantics.

The actor receives the latent command, root-orientation error, base angular velocity, measured joint positions and velocities, and the previous action, while deliberately excluding global root position and root linear velocity. The critic additionally receives privileged simulation information including root-position error, full body-link positions and orientations, and root linear velocity, and is removed for deployment.

The total objective combines the policy loss and multimodal autoencoder loss. The policy term uses a PPO-style clipped surrogate objective with actor, value, and entropy components, and the experiments state that the model is optimized with RAD.

Tracking rewards cover root velocity, root orientation, body position, body orientation, body linear velocity, and body angular velocity, with weights 0.5, 0.5, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0, and 1.0. Regularization includes action-rate, joint-limit, and collision penalties with weights -0.1, -10.0, and -0.1, while the exponential reward scale parameters are not reported.

The curriculum divides trajectories into one-second segments, maintains an EMA of termination failure rate as difficulty, and samples with P_final=αP_uniform+(1-α)clip(P_failure,0,P_max). The ablation uses α_min=0.2 and P_max=0.05; the EMA coefficient, α schedule, and post-clipping normalization are not specified.

Sim-to-Real training randomizes friction, external pushes, base center of mass, base mass, default joint positions, and observation noise for orientation, angular velocity, joint position, and joint velocity. The text also mentions link mass, inertia, joint damping, and motor strength, but their ranges are absent from the table.

Training uses LAFAN1 and 100STYLE, with the OMOMO test subset used for unseen-motion evaluation. Curriculum, data-scale, and network-size ablations are trained for 50000 iterations on four RTX 4090 GPUs. The standard and large MLP configurations are 512-256-128 and 1024-512-256, but the main-model wall-clock training cost is not reported.

On the training datasets, M3imic reaches 99.54% success, 46.05 mm MPKPE, 0.112 rad MPJAE, and 0.256 m/s root-velocity error. On OMOMO, the robot-reference mode obtains the lowest M3imic MPKPE and MPJAE at 71.52 mm and 0.139 rad, while the end-effector mode achieves the highest success rate at 98.42% with slightly higher tracking errors.

In real-world optical-motion-capture experiments, the robot-reference and end-effector modes obtain MPKPE values of 41.63 mm and 43.22 mm and MPJAE values of 0.095 rad and 0.105 rad. The number of trials, variance, real-world success rate, end-to-end latency, control frequency, and inference hardware are not reported.

zh.title: DynaRetarget: Dynamically-Feasible Retargeting using Sampling-Based Trajectory Optimization
zh.authors: Victor Dhédin, Ilyass Taouil, Shafeef Omar, Dian Yu, Kun Tao, Angela Dai, Majid Khadiv
zh.institutions: Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI), Technical University of Munich (TUM), Germany
zh.takeaway: 以运动学重定向为初值，在 MuJoCo 中用采样轨迹优化搜索 PD 目标，生成动力学精炼后的训练参考。
zh.mainContent: DynaRetarget 用运动学参考初始化物理轨迹优化，在 MuJoCo 中通过 CEM / SBTO 搜索 PD-target 序列。优化时逐步扩展时域，以跟踪误差、物理状态和约束反馈修正原参考，再将实际物理 rollout 用于 PPO tracker 训练。它把动力学修正放在离线数据生成阶段，每条新参考都运行优化。
innovations: 将物理 rollout 引入重定向数据精炼。
通过逐步扩展时域的采样优化处理长动作。
implementation: 运动学参考提供初值与跟踪目标；优化变量是 PD-target 序列，仿真器生成状态和代价。
CEM / SBTO 对候选序列进行采样、物理 rollout、评分与分布更新。
优化后的物理轨迹作为下游 PPO 的参考；部署由训练好的 tracker 闭环执行。

en.title: DynaRetarget: Dynamically-Feasible Retargeting using Sampling-Based Trajectory Optimization
en.authors: Victor Dhédin, Ilyass Taouil, Shafeef Omar, Dian Yu, Kun Tao, Angela Dai, Majid Khadiv
en.institutions: Munich Institute of Robotics and Machine Intelligence (MIRMI), Technical University of Munich (TUM), Germany
en.takeaway: Starts from kinematic retargeting and searches PD targets with sampling-based trajectory optimization in MuJoCo to produce dynamically refined references.
en.mainContent: DynaRetarget initializes physical trajectory optimization from kinematic references and searches PD-target sequences with CEM / SBTO in MuJoCo. A progressively extended horizon uses tracking and physical feedback to refine the reference, and the resulting rollouts train a PPO tracker. Dynamic refinement runs offline for each new reference.
innovations: Uses physical rollouts to refine retargeted data.
Handles long motions through sampling optimization with progressively extended horizons.
implementation: Kinematic references provide initialization and tracking targets; PD-target sequences are optimized, while simulation produces states and costs.
CEM / SBTO samples candidate sequences, rolls them out physically, scores them, and updates the search distribution.
Refined physical trajectories become PPO references, and the trained tracker supplies feedback execution.

zh.title: Kinodynamic Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Locomotion via Multi-Contact Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization
zh.authors: Xiaoyu Zhang, Steven Haener, Varun Madabushi, Maegan Tucker
zh.institutions: Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, USA
zh.takeaway: 从同步 MoCap 与地面反力估计姿态和接触日程，再用全身动力学 NLP 修正机器人参考轨迹。
zh.mainContent: KDMR 从同步 MoCap marker 与地面反力估计人体运动和 heel / toe 接触日程，再以多接触全身动力学 NLP 修正机器人动作。优化后的参考将接触与动力学信息带入下游 BeyondMimic 训练。方法针对每段序列离线求解，连接人体数据与物理跟踪控制。
innovations: 核心创新：将 humanoid motion retargeting 表述为预给定 heel/toe 多接触日程下的全身动力学轨迹优化，在参考姿态跟踪之外显式加入浮动基刚体动力学、接触点驻留、摩擦和驱动力限制。
关键设计：利用同步 GRF 的竖直双峰形态识别 heel-only、flat-foot 与 toe-only 阶段，并将质量缩放后的单脚合力分解为 heel/toe 接触力变量，使优化能够表达自然的 heel-to-toe roll。
工程组合与验证：以 OpenSim 人体 IK、差分机器人 IK 和动力学 NLP 组成离线数据生成链，并用 BeyondMimic 下游策略训练比较说明动力学参考数据可能降低策略补偿非物理伪影的负担；OpenSim、CasADi、Pinocchio 和 BeyondMimic 本身均为继承组件。
implementation: 输入为同步的光学 marker 三维轨迹与测力板 GRF；OpenSim inverse kinematics 每个 keyframe 求人体骨架配置，再通过人体 forward kinematics 生成 hip、knee、ankle 等目标 frame 位姿。
接触预处理以竖直 GRF 的 mid-stance dip 为中心确定 flat-foot 窗口，其前后非零 GRF 时段分别标为 heel-only 和 toe-only；GRF 按 robot/human 质量比缩放，并满足单脚合力等于 heel 与 toe 力之和。该启发式针对 steady-state walking。
差分 IK 在速度层最小化机器人 frame 速度与人体目标 frame 速度的加权误差，并满足关节位置和速度边界，输出动力学阶段使用的参考/初始轨迹 \(\mathbf q^{\mathrm{ref}}\)。
动力学阶段在离散时域内联合优化机器人配置、速度、驱动力和四个 heel/toe 三维接触力；加速度是独立变量还是由离散关系导出。约束包括浮动基刚体动力学、stance 点零空间速度与加速度、正法向力、线性摩擦金字塔、关节/力矩边界和梯形积分；swing 点接触力设为零。
代价包含 base/reference tracking、leg joint tracking、相邻速度差、相邻 stance 接触力差、驱动力正则和 stance 点竖直高度软惩罚。论文给出 \(w_v=10^{-3}\)、\(w_\lambda=10^{-4}\)、\(w_\tau=10^{-4}\)、\(w_c=10^3\)，以及 base 和双腿关节的对角权重。
NLP 使用 CasADi 构造，Pinocchio 计算运动学和刚体动力学，目标机器人为 Unitree G1。每条新序列离线求解。
下游使用 BeyondMimic 默认超参数；KDMR 与 GMR 各进行五次随机种子训练，在相同迭代预算下报告 mean reward 和 value loss 的均值与标准差。
公式存在重要歧义：摘要所称 contact complementarity 在正文中实际表现为外部给定的二值接触日程与分模式约束，未展示标准 gap-force 互补条件；展示的 NLP 也未写出源 GRF tracking loss。论文称为梯形积分的两式使用相邻导数之差而非标准的和，不能确认是排版错误还是实际实现。

en.title: Kinodynamic Motion Retargeting for Humanoid Locomotion via Multi-Contact Whole-Body Trajectory Optimization
en.authors: Xiaoyu Zhang, Steven Haener, Varun Madabushi, Maegan Tucker
en.institutions: Georgia Institute of Technology, Atlanta, GA, USA
en.takeaway: Estimates poses and contact schedules from synchronized mocap and ground-reaction forces, then refines robot references with whole-body dynamic NLP.
en.mainContent: KDMR estimates human motion and heel/toe contact schedules from synchronized mocap markers and ground-reaction forces, then refines robot motion with multi-contact whole-body dynamic NLP. The references bring contact and dynamics information into downstream BeyondMimic training. Each sequence is solved offline, connecting human data with physical tracking.
innovations: Core novelty: formulate humanoid motion retargeting as whole-body dynamic trajectory optimization under a prescribed heel/toe multi-contact schedule, explicitly adding floating-base rigid-body dynamics, stationary contact-point conditions, friction, and actuation limits beyond pose tracking.

Key design: use the double-peaked vertical GRF profile to identify heel-only, flat-foot, and toe-only phases, and decompose the mass-scaled net foot force into heel and toe contact-force variables so that the optimizer can represent a natural heel-to-toe roll.

Engineering integration and validation: combine OpenSim human IK, differential robot IK, and a dynamics NLP into an offline data-generation pipeline, then use BeyondMimic training to test whether dynamically feasible references reduce the policy's burden of compensating for nonphysical artifacts; OpenSim, CasADi, Pinocchio, and BeyondMimic are inherited components rather than new algorithms.
implementation: Inputs are synchronized 3D optical-marker trajectories and force-plate GRFs. OpenSim inverse kinematics solves the human skeleton configuration at every keyframe, and human-model forward kinematics produces target-frame poses such as hip, knee, and ankle. The OpenSim model version, marker weights, complete frame list, and human-to-robot link mapping are not specified.

Contact preprocessing centers a flat-foot window around the mid-stance dip of the vertical GRF and labels the preceding and succeeding nonzero-GRF intervals as heel-only and toe-only. GRF is scaled by the robot-to-human mass ratio, with each foot's resultant represented as the sum of heel and toe forces. This heuristic is specific to steady-state walking.

Differential IK minimizes weighted task-space velocity errors between corresponding human and robot frames under joint-position and velocity bounds, producing the reference/initial trajectory \(\mathbf q^{\mathrm{ref}}\) for the dynamic stage.

The dynamic stage jointly optimizes robot configurations, velocities, actuation, and four 3D heel/toe contact forces over a discretized horizon; the paper is unclear whether acceleration is an independent variable or derived from the transcription. Constraints include floating-base rigid-body dynamics, zero spatial velocity and acceleration for stance points, positive normal force, a linearized friction pyramid, joint/torque bounds, and trapezoidal integration; swing contact forces are set to zero.

The objective includes base and leg-joint reference tracking, adjacent-velocity smoothing, adjacent stance-force smoothing, actuation regularization, and a soft vertical-height penalty on stance points. Reported weights include \(w_v=10^{-3}\), \(w_\lambda=10^{-4}\), \(w_\tau=10^{-4}\), and \(w_c=10^3\), together with diagonal base and bilateral leg-joint weights.
Builds the NLP with CasADi and computes kinematics and rigid-body dynamics with Pinocchio for Unitree G1. Each new sequence is solved offline.
Uses default BeyondMimic settings and five seeded runs each for KDMR and GMR, reporting reward and value-loss means and standard deviations under the same iteration budget.

Important formulation ambiguities remain: the abstract's contact-complementarity claim is implemented in the shown equations as an externally prescribed binary contact schedule with mode-dependent constraints, not a standard gap-force complementarity condition; the displayed NLP also contains no explicit source-GRF tracking loss. The equations labeled as trapezoidal integration use differences rather than the standard sums of adjacent derivatives, so it is unclear whether this is a typographical error or the implemented form.

zh.title: MotionDisco: Motion Discovery for Extreme Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
zh.authors: Ilyass Taouil, Michal Ciebielski, Shafeef Omar, Haizhou Zhao, Angela Dai, Aaron M. Johnson, Majid Khadiv
zh.institutions: Technical University of Munich; New York University; Carnegie Mellon University
zh.takeaway: LLM 搜索离散接触方案，运动学与动力学优化生成连续参考，再由 RL tracker 在真机上执行。
zh.mainContent: MotionDisco 面向无现成人类示范的长时域、富接触人形 loco-manipulation，目标是在不依赖遥操作或 human-to-humanoid motion retargeting 的情况下从零发现动作。给定完全已知的文本场景表示与任务目标，Claude Opus 4.7 在进化树中修改可执行的接触计划程序；顺序运动学优化先做廉价几何筛选，随后接触显式 TO 联合求解机器人—物体状态、控制、接触 wrench 与各接触阶段时长，并把数值和文本反馈返回搜索。论文在 8 个任务上报告完整方法均找到有效方案，且相较单次 LLM 调用以及无文本反馈的进化搜索获得更高的有效方案比例和更低的 TO cost；各任务首次有效解耗时为 1.34–7.49 分钟。发现的轨迹随后作为参考训练带 domain randomization 的 DeepMimic-style RL 跟踪策略并 zero-shot 部署到真机，但系统假设场景预先已知，且接触和物体模型受到明显限制。
innovations: 把长时域 loco-manipulation 表示成可执行程序形式的离散接触模式序列，并采用基于 ShinkaEvolve 的 LLM 引导进化树搜索；island 子群、inspiration sampling、novelty rejection 和多种 mutation 共同维持探索多样性。
设计分层 kinodynamic evaluator：先用忽略动力学的顺序运动学优化快速剔除几何不可行计划，再对通过者运行完整接触显式 TO；系统还定位最长可行前缀和首个失败接触转换，并将其转为文本反馈指导下一轮局部修补。
将自动接触方案发现、连续动力学轨迹生成和 RL 跟踪部署连成闭环。论文声称这是首个完全通过自动进化搜索发现并部署长时域人形 loco-manipulation 技能的工作，同时能够在一次搜索中产生多种不同的可行接触方案。
implementation: 搜索输入为场景 \(\mathcal{S}\) 与目标 \(\mathcal{G}\)：\(\mathcal{S}\) 是包含每个物体标签、世界位置和尺寸的已知文本场景，\(\mathcal{G}\) 可同时指定目标接触关系与机器人或物体的连续目标位姿。LLM 输出 Python 接触计划程序，程序执行后得到离散接触模式序列 \(\mathcal{C}\)，而不是输出 policy action 或逐帧轨迹。
每个搜索节点保存接触计划程序、执行得到的接触序列、标量 score、可选文本反馈和 offspring count。所有 LLM 组件使用 Claude Opus 4.7；mutation 类型为 targeted diff edit、full rewrite 和 crossover，采样概率分别为 0.6、0.3 和 0.1。
顺序运动学优化忽略动力学，仅检查碰撞规避、构型限制与接触转换一致性；若完整序列失败，程序反复缩短序列以找出最长可行前缀并报告首个失败 mode 或 transition。该阶段采用 direct multiple shooting transcription，并由 acados 求解。
对运动学可行的固定接触序列，TO 联合优化机器人—物体状态轨迹 \(x(\cdot)\)、控制轨迹 \(u(\cdot)\)、接触 wrench 以及各 mode 的持续时间 \(\bar{T}_{0:K-1}\)，同时约束动力学、接触、碰撞和状态/控制限位。TO 采用 direct multiple shooting transcription，并由 Hippo 求解。

TO 的抽象目标为 \(\int_0^T \phi(x(t),u(t))\,dt+\phi_T(x(T))+w_TT\)。用于评价接触方案的 cost 为 \(J(\mathcal{C})=\sum_i\lVert r(x_i,u_i,c_{s(i)})\rVert_1+w_j\sum_i\lVert\dddot q_i\rVert^2\)，即约束残差与 jerk 正则之和；运动学失败的节点不运行 TO，并获得零 score。

评测包含 Banana、Box Stacking、Climb Table w/ Box、Long-Distance Pick & Place、Move Through Clutter、两项 Parkour Pick & Place 和 Under-Table Pick & Place 共 8 个任务。完整方法在全部任务中找到有效方案；论文把“通过顺序运动学检查且 TO 收敛”定义为 valid plan。
部署阶段将 TO 轨迹作为 reference，在仿真中用 DeepMimic-style rewards 和 domain randomization 训练 RL motion-tracking policy，再 zero-shot 迁移到真实人形机器人。
关键限制是场景几何与初始状态必须预先已知且没有 perception；当前规划器只支持矩形 patch 上的 unilateral sticking contact，被操作对象限于 rigid box-like geometry，不支持滑动接触、关节物体、自由形状物体或软体。

en.title: MotionDisco: Motion Discovery for Extreme Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
en.authors: Ilyass Taouil, Michal Ciebielski, Shafeef Omar, Haizhou Zhao, Angela Dai, Aaron M. Johnson, Majid Khadiv
en.institutions: Technical University of Munich; New York University; Carnegie Mellon University
en.takeaway: An LLM searches discrete contact plans, kinematic and dynamic optimization produce references, and an RL tracker executes them on the real robot.
en.mainContent: MotionDisco targets long-horizon, contact-rich humanoid loco-manipulation without requiring teleoperation or human-to-humanoid motion retargeting. Given a fully known textual scene representation and task goal, Claude Opus 4.7 mutates executable contact-plan programs in an evolutionary tree; sequential kinematic optimization provides a cheap geometric filter, after which contact-explicit TO jointly solves robot-object states, controls, contact wrenches, and contact-stage durations while returning numerical and textual feedback to the search. Across eight tasks, the complete method found valid plans in every scenario and reported higher valid-plan rates and lower TO costs than a single LLM call and evolutionary search without textual feedback; time to the first valid solution ranged from 1.34 to 7.49 minutes. The discovered trajectories are then used as references for DeepMimic-style RL tracking with domain randomization and zero-shot hardware deployment, although the method assumes a known scene and uses restricted contact and object models.
innovations: It represents long-horizon loco-manipulation as executable programs over discrete contact-mode sequences and applies ShinkaEvolve-based LLM-guided evolutionary tree search, using island subpopulations, inspiration sampling, novelty rejection, and multiple mutation operators to preserve diversity.

It introduces a layered kinodynamic evaluator: dynamics-free sequential kinematic optimization first rejects geometrically infeasible plans, and full contact-explicit TO evaluates the survivors. The evaluator identifies the longest feasible prefix and first failing contact mode or transition, then converts this information into textual feedback for local repair in subsequent mutations.

It closes the loop from automated contact-plan discovery through continuous dynamically feasible trajectory generation to RL tracking on hardware. The paper claims the first deployment of long-horizon humanoid loco-manipulation skills discovered entirely through automated evolutionary search, while producing multiple distinct feasible solutions within a single run.
implementation: The search takes a scene \(\mathcal{S}\) and goal \(\mathcal{G}\). The known textual scene lists each object's label, world position, and dimensions, while the goal can include desired discrete contacts and continuous robot or object poses. The LLM outputs a Python contact-plan program whose execution produces a discrete mode sequence \(\mathcal{C}\), not policy actions or a frame-level trajectory.

Each tree node stores the contact-plan program, its executed contact sequence, a scalar score, optional textual feedback, and an offspring count. All LLM components use Claude Opus 4.7. The targeted-diff, full-rewrite, and crossover mutations are sampled with probabilities 0.6, 0.3, and 0.1, respectively.

Sequential kinematic optimization ignores dynamics and checks collision avoidance, configuration limits, and contact-transition consistency. When a full sequence fails, the system repeatedly shortens it to recover the longest feasible prefix and report the first failing mode or transition. This stage uses a direct multiple-shooting transcription solved with acados.

For a kinematically feasible fixed contact sequence, TO jointly optimizes the robot-object state trajectory \(x(\cdot)\), control trajectory \(u(\cdot)\), contact wrenches, and mode durations \(\bar{T}_{0:K-1}\), subject to dynamics, contact, collision, and state/control-limit constraints. The TO also uses direct multiple shooting and is solved with Hippo.

The abstract TO objective is \(\int_0^T \phi(x(t),u(t))\,dt+\phi_T(x(T))+w_TT\). Contact-plan evaluation uses \(J(\mathcal{C})=\sum_i\lVert r(x_i,u_i,c_{s(i)})\rVert_1+w_j\sum_i\lVert\dddot q_i\rVert^2\), combining constraint residuals and jerk regularization; a kinematically infeasible node skips TO and receives zero score.

Evaluation covers eight tasks: Banana, Box Stacking, Climb Table with Box, Long-Distance Pick and Place, Move Through Clutter, two Parkour Pick and Place variants, and Under-Table Pick and Place. The complete method found a valid plan for every task; a plan is considered valid when it passes sequential kinematic feasibility and TO converges.

For deployment, the TO trajectory becomes a reference for an RL motion-tracking policy trained in simulation with DeepMimic-style rewards and domain randomization, followed by zero-shot transfer to a real humanoid.

The method assumes known scene geometry and initial state and contains no perception. Its planner currently supports only unilateral sticking contacts on rectangular patches and rigid box-like manipulated objects, excluding sliding contact, articulated objects, free-form objects, and deformable objects.

zh.title: DeepLoco: Dynamic Locomotion Skills Using Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning
zh.authors: Xue Bin Peng, Glen Berseth, KangKang Yin, Michiel van de Panne
zh.institutions: University of British Columbia；National University of Singapore
zh.takeaway: 用未来脚点与躯干朝向连接高层规划和低层反馈：先学会执行脚步，再学会按地形选择脚步。
zh.mainContent: DeepLoco 以未来两步脚点和躯干朝向连接高层规划与低层反馈。先训练低层策略把这些目标转为关节 PD 动作，再冻结低层，为不同环境任务训练选择脚点的高层控制器。两层接口把长期地形决策与高频平衡执行分开，在仿真中完成障碍和复杂地形运动。
innovations: 核心创新：用“未来两步二维脚点＋下一步躯干朝向”作为高层与低层之间具有物理语义的接口，使高层只负责步级规划，低层只负责高频平衡、摆腿和落脚。
核心训练设计：先独立训练 LLC，再冻结 LLC 训练任务专用 HLC，避免联合训练时 LLC 持续变化导致高层所面对的等效动力学非平稳。层级强化学习本身并非本文首次提出，贡献主要在这一具体接口、训练顺序和完整系统。
系统贡献：同一个脚点接口同时支持路径跟随、静态与动态避障以及通过足部接触完成的足球运球，说明它可以作为多种环境感知 locomotion 任务的动作抽象。
关键辅助设计：用参考动作奖励降低三维双足行走的探索难度，并通过四槽双线性相位变换显式区分不同 gait phase；这些设计对训练很重要，但不是层级方法的核心创新。
有限的模块复用：不同风格 LLC 可由名义 LLC 微调得到，高层也可在更换 LLC 后继续微调；实验支持已有策略可作为有效初始化，但不支持 HLC 与 LLC 可以任意、无损地即插即用。
implementation: 数据准备：LLC 可以使用手工 keyframed walk cycle，也可以使用约 7 秒的 walking/turning mocap。后者被切成约 10 个单步片段，统一为右脚支撑并 time-warp 到 0.5 秒；训练时根据当前支撑腿镜像。最近邻选择器在每步开始时选取与目标脚点和朝向最匹配的参考片段。
LLC 输入输出：低层状态共 110 维，包含相对 root 表达的 link 位置、旋转、线速度和角速度、双足接触以及固定相位；另接收未来两步脚点和下一步躯干朝向。LLC 以 30 Hz 输出 22 维关节 PD target，而不是直接输出力矩。
参考动作的边界：参考片段只用于选择模仿目标和计算训练奖励，不作为 LLC 在线输入。运行时可以删除 mocap、参考片段选择器和模仿奖励，因此 LLC 不是 reference-conditioned tracker。
LLC 奖励：奖励由关节姿态、关节速度、root 高度、质心速度、摆动脚与支撑脚位置以及 heading 项组成。参考项维持动作风格，脚点和 heading 项让策略能够偏离参考并服从高层命令。
学习算法：两层均使用带最近 50k transitions 经验回放的 CACLA 式 actor–critic。critic 学习一步 bootstrap value；只有样本确实加入了探索噪声且 TD error 为正时，actor 才向该探索动作靠近。探索采用固定对角 Gaussian，并通过 Bernoulli 变量决定当前动作是否加入噪声；部署时只使用 actor 均值。
网络与优化：LLC actor 在四槽双线性相位变换后接 512、256 单元 ReLU 层并输出 22 维动作。优化器为带 0.9 momentum 的 SGD；actor 使用 0.0005 的 L2 weight decay，critic 不使用 weight decay。这是策略正则化的辅助技巧，不是核心贡献。
HLC 输入输出：静态环境任务的高层状态包含角色特征和角色中心坐标系下的 32×32 高度图，报告总维数为 1129；动态障碍任务改用记录障碍水平速度的 velocity map。HLC 还接收任务目标，并以 2 Hz 输出两个二维脚点和一个 heading，由接口定义可知共 5 维。
HLC 网络：地图依次经过 16 个 5×5、32 个 4×4、32 个 3×3 卷积滤波器和一个 128 单元全连接层，再与角色特征及任务目标拼接，经过 512、256 单元 ReLU 层输出脚点计划。
两阶段训练：名义 LLC 约训练 6M iterations；随后完全冻结 LLC，为路径、障碍或足球等每项任务分别训练一个 HLC，约 1M iterations。论文报告在 16 核 CPU 上 LLC 训练约 2 天、每个 HLC 约 7 天。
运行闭环：HLC 每 0.5 秒生成一次落脚计划，LLC 在该计划下约执行 15 次更新；stable PD 将关节目标变成受限力矩，Bullet 以 3 kHz 推进物理仿真。运行时保留 HLC actor、LLC actor、固定相位、状态和地图提取、动作裁剪、PD 与物理系统；critic、replay buffer、reward、参考动作和探索噪声全部删除。
实验结论：Figure 11 中，分层版本在路径跟随和足球任务上明显优于作者的单层版本；Figure 8 表明多个参考片段能显著改善 LLC 学习。名义步态可承受论文所测的 200 N 前向推力、210 N 侧向推力和 16% 上坡，但实验没有多随机种子误差条、外部方法基线或真实机器人验证。
关键限制：系统依赖仿真真值本体状态、足接触、局部地图和球状态；默认 LLC 只会恒速行走与转向，不会停止，导致动态避障 NCR 仅为 0.18。每个新任务仍需训练新的 HLC，能力范围受 LLC skill repertoire 和脚点训练分布限制。
复现注意：Algorithm 1 的 critic target 与正文公式冲突，可能重复减去一次 value；双线性相位公式的最后一个槽也疑似把 Phi3 误印成重复的 Phi2。论文还缺少角色完整惯量与碰撞体、精确归一化参数、逐维探索方差、mocap 索引和 retarget 脚本等信息。

en.title: DeepLoco: Dynamic Locomotion Skills Using Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning
en.authors: Xue Bin Peng, Glen Berseth, KangKang Yin, Michiel van de Panne
en.institutions: University of British Columbia; National University of Singapore
en.takeaway: Connects high-level planning and low-level feedback through future foot placements and torso orientation: first learn to execute steps, then select them for terrain.
en.mainContent: DeepLoco connects planning and feedback through two future foot placements and torso orientation. It first trains a low-level policy to produce joint PD targets, then freezes it and trains task-specific high-level foot-placement policies. The interface separates longer-horizon terrain decisions from balance execution for simulated obstacle and terrain tasks.
innovations: Core innovation: a physically meaningful interface consisting of two future 2D footsteps and a desired torso heading separates step-level planning in the HLC from high-frequency balance, swing-leg control, and landing in the LLC.

Core training design: the LLC is trained first and then frozen while task-specific HLCs are learned, avoiding the non-stationary effective dynamics faced by the HLC when the LLC changes during joint training.
